learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and aptitudes in the field of Mechanical Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert opinions, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to organize and plan within the company, and other institutions and organizations.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment, and solidarity spirit.
Ability to work in a team.
Adequate knowledge of the concept of business, institutional and legal framework of the company. Organization and management of companies.
Understand the concept of a company, types of companies, and the environment in which it operates.
Be able to understand the different subsystems that integrate the company.
Understand the principles of business organization and management.

syllabus_topics: Functioning of economic activity and types of markets
Concept and objectives of the company
Types of company: economic, organizational, and legal criteria
Asset and results analysis for decision making
Valuation of investment and financing projects
teaching_methods: Case analysis (reading documents and watching videos)
Presentation of individual or group assignments
assessment_rules: The ordinary assessment consists of a final theoretical-practical exam (EX.ORD, max 6.5 points, minimum 40% to pass) and three evaluable practices (P1, P2, P3, max 1 point each) plus participation (P, max 0.5 points). A minimum of 1.4 points is required in the sum of P1, P2, P3, and P (40% of 3.5 points). The final grade is EX.ORD + P1 + P2 + P3 + P. To pass, all minimums must be met and a total of at least 5 points achieved. If all minimums are met but the total is less than 5 points, the course is failed with the calculated grade. If the total is over 5 points but a minimum was not reached, the final grade is 4 points (fail). For extraordinary exams, students can retake EX.EXTR (theoretical-practical, max 6.5 points, min 40%) and/or EX.PR (practical, max 3.5 points, min 40%), with previous valid scores being carried over.
